source_capture: Read-only extraction from the same installed SIF/overlay and container environment as the measured job, using importlib module discovery without importing the GPU engine. File hashes and source line numbers below identify the inspected bytes.

observations.output_handler_exception: EngineDeadError at 22:01:45 after MPClient resource cleanup
observations.resource_tracker_warnings: At shutdown, resource_tracker reported semaphore/shared-memory objects to clean up. Persistent IPC leakage was not measured.

causal_analysis.status: confirmed by pinned source and CPU reproduction
causal_analysis.finding: The configured default shutdown timeout is zero. The process manager sends SIGTERM and immediately reaches the forced process-tree termination path, giving the engine no cleanup wait. CPU reproduction killed a live cleanup worker with SIGKILL at zero timeout; a one-second grace let that worker finish.

causal_analysis.status: confirmed source order; consistent with observed traceback
causal_analysis.finding: AsyncLLM.shutdown stops the engine client before cancelling its output-handler task. The task observes EngineDeadError while intentional engine teardown is in progress and logs it as an exception.

causal_analysis.status: inference supported by timestamps, forced-kill log and Slurm cancellation semantics
causal_analysis.finding: Immediate engine/process-tree termination and job-wide cancellation can close the head-node TCPStore before peer NCCL watchdogs finish. Their recvValue/Broken pipe/DistNetworkError messages follow the cancellation, rather than the serving checks.

decision.reason: The CLI down command requests immediate allocation cancellation. All completed requests passed, the model was removed from the router, endpoints and keys were removed, and every allocation/step ended. The observed warnings do not demonstrate a serving failure or an unreleased allocation. Document the abort contract and diagnostic distinction; preserve the measured runtime/serve bytes.
decision.limit: Graceful draining and warning-free teardown are not established. A positive vLLM timeout alone is not a validated remedy for simultaneous Slurm cancellation; a drain feature needs coordinated signal handling and another multi-node GPU run. Unexpected occurrences before an operator stop or while requests are serving still require failure investigation.
